chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, both together, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He said: I asked him about the mouse, the scorpion, and similar creatures that fall into water and come out alive — can one drink from that water and perform wudu from it? He said: It [the water] is poured out three times, and a small amount and a large amount are of the same ruling, then one may drink from it and perform wudu from it — except for the gecko (wazagh), for nothing it falls into may be benefited from.

Al-Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: What this report contains regarding the ruling on the gecko and the command to pour away what it falls into is interpreted as a type of legal dislikedness (karahah), based on the indication of the preceding report, and contradiction between reports is not permissible.

key_terms.الكَرَاهِيَةِ: legal dislikedness (karahah) — a fiqh ruling below the threshold of prohibition (haram)
key_terms.الوَزَغِ: gecko (wazagh) — a lizard-like creature whose contact with water renders it permanently unusable
key_terms.يُسكَبُ: to pour out — the prescribed purification act performed three times

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on water in which a mouse, scorpion, or gecko has fallen according to Imam al-Sadiq's hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules on the ritual status of water into which mice, scorpions, or similar creatures have fallen and come out alive: pouring the water out three times renders it permissible for drinking and wudu regardless of quantity, with the sole exception of the gecko (wazagh). Sheikh al-Tusi appends a jurisprudential note interpreting the gecko exception as a legal dislikedness (karahah) rather than outright prohibition, harmonizing this report with a preceding narration and upholding the principle that authentic reports may not contradict one another.
